review_notes: I read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes and no simp lemmas, and `OriginalNodeReady` and `guardedNodeLaw` are plain defs. The main theorem and `original_ready_sparse` are proved by explicit rewriting and linear arithmetic, so I found no rewrite cycle, bad orientation, or competing rules in this file. The one real simp-interface gap is the missing equation lemmas for `guardedNodeLaw`. I checked its uses in GuardedNode.lean, GuardedNodeEncoder.lean and GuardedNodeOriginal.lean, and the neighbouring `guardedNode_encode_none` lemma. I did not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested. I did not recommend a simp attribute on `OriginalNodeReady`: its unfoldings (ReadyRefinement.lean line 47, OriginalReadiness.lean line 22) are one-off, and OriginalReadiness.lean already has a negation iff.

findings.problem: `guardedNodeLaw` is a dite on `OriginalNodeReady` with no equation lemmas. Every consumer has to unfold the whole definition, including the six `letI` instance blocks, before it can use either branch. GuardedNode.lean does `simpa only [guardedNodeLaw,dite_eq_left hready] using hf`. GuardedNodeOriginal.lean does `unfold guardedNodeLaw; split_ifs`. GuardedNodeEncoder.lean does `unfold guardedNodeEncoded guardedNodeLaw; split_ifs`. The sibling `guardedNodeEncoded` already has a not-ready lemma, `guardedNode_encode_none`, but `guardedNodeLaw` has no counterpart. The expected normal form of `guardedNodeLaw … = pureLaw none` when `¬OriginalNodeReady` is therefore not available to `simp`. The ready branch has no lemma either, so call sites expose the raw `dite` and the `let hA := … let hnA := …` proof terms.
findings.proposed_change: Right after the definition, add two equation lemmas. First, `guardedNodeLaw_of_not_ready (hr : ¬OriginalNodeReady A₀ UA B₀ UB δ τ) : guardedNodeLaw pred σ hσ hq hd A₀ UA B₀ UB hA₀ hB₀ c δ τ M hδ = pureLaw none`, proved by `simp only [guardedNodeLaw, hr, ↓reduceDIte]`, which is the proof style `guardedNode_encode_none` already uses. Mark it `@[simp]` if you want `simp` to use it, since the hypothesis `hr` is dischargeable from context. Second, `guardedNodeLaw_of_ready (hr : OriginalNodeReady …) : guardedNodeLaw … = finiteNodeOutput pred (A₀∩UA) UA (B₀∩UB) UB … c M`, stating the Fin arguments with the same `reverseLength_universal_bound` proofs. Then replace the unfold-and-`dite_eq_left` proofs at the three call sites with `rw [guardedNodeLaw_of_ready hr]` or `rw [guardedNodeLaw_of_not_ready hr]`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical rewrite for each branch and no longer unfold the definition with its instance setup. The ready/not-ready case split is stated once. Both laws (`guardedNodeLaw`, `guardedNodeEncoded`) then expose the same interface, so later proofs about the guarded node stay stable if the definition's internal structure changes.
